title: Monaco vs Marseille: Crucial Ligue 1 clash stirs French Championship
seoTitle: Monaco vs Marseille: Filipe Luís' debut test
subtitle: The second-round match marks Filipe Luís' first major test as a coach in Europe and promises a fight for the top spot.
excerpt: The Monaco vs Olympique de Marseille clash is trending, representing one of the most anticipated games of the second round of the French Championship.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
One of the most anticipated clashes of the second round of the French Championship, between Monaco and Olympique de Marseille, takes place this Sunday, the 30th, at 3:45 PM (Brasília time). The match, which will be played at the Stade Louis-II, attracts special attention for being the first major test for Filipe Luís in charge of the home team, and for pitting two teams against each other that started the season with impressive victories in Ligue 1.

Crucial duel for the lead

Monaco and Olympique de Marseille face off at a key moment, both having earned three points in the first round. Monaco sits in fifth place, while Marseille appears in second. A victory could take either team to the top of the championship table, reinforcing expectations for the new season.

Filipe Luís' challenge at Monaco

Signed in July, 41-year-old Filipe Luís signed a contract until June 2028 and begins his first experience as a coach in European football. He arrives at Monaco with the goal of returning the club to a more prominent position in European competitions. During the pre-season, Monaco showed capability by defeating Liverpool 3-2. In Ligue 1, the team started with a 1-0 win over Le Havre, with a goal from Eric Dier.

Monaco also came off a 4-1 thrashing of Górnik in the Conference League, securing qualification for the League Phase of the European competition. The sequence of matches and the absences of players like Takumi Minamino, Mohammed Salisu, and Ansu Fati, alongside doubts about Matthis Abline and Folarin Balogun, may influence Filipe Luís' choices for the clash. However, the home team has a favorable record against Marseille at the Stade Louis-II, having won the last three French Championship matches at their stadium.

Olympique de Marseille seeks the top spot

On the other side, Olympique de Marseille, managed by Bruno Genesio, had an even more promising start. The team thrashed Strasbourg 4-0 at the Vélodrome, finishing the first round at the top of the championship. Amine Gouiri, Keyliane Abdallah, and Pierre-Emile Højbjerg scored in the victory that reinforced expectations surrounding the club.

For the duel against Monaco, Marseille will have at least one significant absence in defense, with Leonardo Balerdi out due to injury. Other absences may include Egan-Riley, Moumbagna, and Igor Paixão, who is in doubt for the clash. Despite the challenges, Marseille sees the game as an opportunity to retake the top of Ligue 1.

Where to watch and probable lineups

The match between Monaco and Olympique de Marseille, this Sunday, the 30th, at 3:45 PM (Brasília time), will have exclusive broadcast on CazéTV.

Probable lineups

  • Monaco: Hradecky; Vanderson, Sané, Eric Dier, and Nazinho; Lamine Camara and Denis Zakaria; Mamadou Coulibaly, Aleksandr Golovin, and Stanis Idumbo; Paris Brunner. Coach: Filipe Luís.
  • Olympique de Marseille: De Lange; Timothy Weah, Nayef Aguerd, Geoffrey Kondogbia, and Emerson Palmieri; Himad Abdelli, Pierre-Emile Højbjerg, and Angel Gomes; Amine Harit, Amine Gouiri, and Igor Paixão. Coach: Bruno Genesio.

With information from VEJA, Gazeta Esportiva, Terra.
